newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes barely changed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes barely changed in quiet trade.

text.p: Precious metals business was very quiet on Monday and featured little more than dealers closing out positions ahead of the Christmas holiday.
"The chances of something happening are relatively slim but, because of that, if there is a move it could be quite vicious," a dealer said.
After Tuesday morning, there will be no gold fix until Friday following London's two-day Christmas holiday.
Gold was fixed at $368.75 per ounce, up five cents from the Monday morning fix and compared with $369.00 on Friday afternoon.
Comex February was quoted at $370.60 up $0.10 at the fixing.
Dealers said the OTC option expiry went off quietly on Friday without creating waves or adding to volatility.
They said the market had run its course for the year and there was little likelihood of a move away from the current $368-$370 range.

"But I'm quite happy to close out positions ahead of Christmas rather than risk it getting jumpy in New York on Thursday (when London is closed)," one dealer said, adding that prices might well be different from now by Friday.
Silver was quiet as well with the price indicated up a cent at $4.84/$4.86.
"There is a chance they may try to move it lower, in which case $4.78 would be the floor. You always expect silver to be more potentially volatile than gold," a dealer said.
Platinum and palladium edged just below Friday's close with platinum 25 cents down at $372.00/$373.00 and palladium met some selling to be down $1.50 at $116.50/$117.50.
